content: Nail abnormalities refer to issues involving the color, shape, texture, or thickness of fingernails or toenails. These changes can arise from various causes, including injury, infection, systemic diseases, exposure to toxins, medications, or aging. Causes of Nail Changes: Injury: Crushing injuries to the nail base or nail bed can result in permanent deformities. Chronic picking or rubbing of the skin behind the nail may lead to a washboard nail appearance. Prolonged exposure to moisture or nail polish can cause nails to peel and become brittle. Infections: Fungal or yeast infections can alter the color, texture, and shape of nails. Bacterial infections may lead to discoloration or painful areas of infection beneath the nail or in the surrounding skin. Severe infections can result in nail loss. Viral warts can distort the nail shape or cause ingrown skin beneath the nail. Certain infections, such as endocarditis (infection of the heart valve), may cause red streaks in the nail bed, known as splinter hemorrhages. Diseases: Conditions that reduce oxygen levels in the blood, such as congenital heart defects or lung diseases (including cancer or infections), can cause clubbing of the nails. Kidney disease can lead to the accumulation of nitrogen waste products in the blood, which may damage nails. Liver disease can also result in nail damage. Thyroid disorders, such as hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism, may cause brittle nails or onycholysis (separation of the nail bed from the nail plate). Severe illnesses or surgeries can cause horizontal depressions in the nails, known as Beau's lines. Psoriasis can lead to pitting, onycholysis, and chronic destruction of the nail plate (nail dystrophy). Other conditions affecting nail appearance include systemic amyloidosis, malnutrition, vitamin deficiencies, and lichen planus. Skin cancers near the nail or fingertip can distort the nail. Subungual melanoma, a potentially fatal cancer, often appears as a dark streak running the length of the nail. Darkening of the cuticle associated with a pigmented streak may indicate an aggressive melanoma. Toxins: Arsenic poisoning can cause white lines and horizontal ridges on the nails. Silver exposure may result in blue discoloration of the nails. Medications: Certain antibiotics can cause the nail to lift from the nail bed. Chemotherapy drugs can interfere with nail growth. Aging: Normal aging processes can affect nail growth and development. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care: Contact a healthcare provider if you notice any of the following: A new or widening dark streak in the nail. Blue nails. Clubbed nails. Distorted nails. Horizontal ridges. Pale nails. White lines. White discoloration beneath the nails. If splinter hemorrhages are present, seek immediate medical attention. Diagnosis: A healthcare provider will examine your nails and ask detailed questions about your symptoms. These questions may include: What is the specific abnormality? Is there an unusual color? If so, what color? Are there red lines running the length of the nail (splinter hemorrhages)? Is the shape abnormal? Has the texture or thickness changed? Are the nails pitted or detached? Are there ridges, and in which direction do they run? Does the fingertip appear enlarged? Is there a lack of luster? Are the nails brittle? Where is the abnormality located? Is it on the hands, feet, or both? Is it on one side or both sides? Is it limited to a specific nail? Are there aggravating factors? Have you had an injury to the nail? Do you bite your nails? Do you chronically pick at or rub your nails or fingers? Are the nails frequently exposed to moisture? Do you use nail polish? Are there any other associated symptoms? Diagnostic tests may include X-rays, blood tests, or laboratory examination of nail samples, depending on the associated symptoms. Prevention: Avoid biting, picking, or tearing at your nails. In severe cases, psychological support may be necessary to stop these behaviors. Keep hangnails trimmed. Wear shoes that do not compress the toes, and always cut nails straight across. To prevent brittle nails, keep them short and avoid nail polish. Use an emollient cream after washing or bathing. Strengthen nails by using biotin supplements and clear nail polish containing protein.
